plan: [This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where truthful bidding is a dominant strategy. With my private value v = $42, bidding my true value maximizes expected payoff regardless of others' strategies. I will bid $42 (allowed to the nearest $0.1). Ties are random but bidding truthfully ensures I win exactly when the second-highest bid is below my value and pay that second price, maximizing long-run profit.]

[This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and no prior history. Bidding your true value is a dominant strategy and maximizes expected payoff. My private value is $29, so I will bid $29. This avoids the risk of losing positive surplus from underbidding and has no downside from overbidding in a Vickrey auction.]

[In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true valuation is a weakly dominant strategy. Other bidders are rational and will bid their values as well. With value $48, bidding 48 maximizes expected profit: if you win you pay the second-highest bid and gain 48 minus that; if you lose you pay nothing. Bids allowed in $0.1 increments; ties resolved randomly. Truthful bidding (48) is optimal for long-run profit maximization.]
